newsitem.title: UK: Oil slips ahead of U.S. inventory data.
newsitem.headline: Oil slips ahead of U.S. inventory data.

text.p: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as dealers sniffed the wind ahead of a key weekly inventory report from the United States.
London March futures for bellwether Brent blend closed down nine cents a barrel at $22.45.

Prices were lower despite a brief fillip from a German newspaper report that the U.S. was contemplating a possible missile strike against Iraq because of Baghdad's continued efforts at missile development.
An advance release from Wednesday's edition of Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said the United States could make a decision this week on whether to launch a strike.
The U.S. State Department said later that it had no "heightened concern" over the situation in Iraq, but refused to comment on the newspaper report.

Traders said they were waiting for the release after markets close on Tuesday of American Petroleum Institute (API) statistics for the latest clue in how oil stocks are shaping up relative to a year ago.

"Distillate (heating oil and diesel) stocks relative to a year-ago are worth watching," said broker Leslie Nicholas at GNI in London. "If the current deficit turns into a surplus there could be a negative psychological impact on the market."
Record refinery operations in the U.S. have helped heating oil inventories recover in recent weeks from a big year-on-year shortfall.
Mild spells of winter weather in the Northeast U.S. and Northwest European heating oil markets also have taken the edge off prices for the petroleum product.
U.S. refiners have taken the opportunity to take plants into maintenance, reducing demand for crude along refinery row on the U.S. Gulf.
Imports into the U.S., easily the world's biggest buyer, have dipped as a result, putting pressure on spot markets in Nigerian, North Sea and Latin American crudes.
Dealers also remained nervous about taking out new long positions on futures markets after Friday's unexpected 66 cent slump on Brent.
"Some people went a bit long in the run up last week and had the stuffing knocked out of them in the end," said a London based trader.
